objects.description: A base class to disable copying for derived classes. Copy constructor and copy assignment are deleted; default destructor; move assignment is noexcept. Has a protected default constructor so it is intended to be used as a base, not instantiated directly.
Enumeration of page rotation angles in degrees (0, 90, 180, 270).
Enumeration selecting a page boundary box: Media, Crop, Bleed, Trim, or Art box.
Enumeration of document permission bits such as printing, changing, copying, adding notes, filling forms, accessibility, assembling, and high-resolution printing.
Enumeration indicating whether comparisons are case-sensitive or case-insensitive.
Alias for a dynamic array of bytes stored as std::vector<char>. Often used for raw data buffers and UTF-8 output from ustring.

UTF-16 string class derived from std::basic_string<char16_t>. Provides conversions to UTF-8 (as byte_array) and Latin-1, and factory methods to construct from UTF-8 and Latin-1. Implicit std::string conversions are intentionally disabled to avoid accidental narrowing or encoding mistakes. Lifetime and memory are managed like std::basic_string; no special destruction is required.
Function pointer type for a debug/error callback that receives a message string and an opaque user pointer.
Alias for rectangle<int>, representing an integer-based rectangle. Same behavior and methods as rectangle<int>.
Alias for rectangle<double>, representing a floating-point rectangle with double precision. Same behavior and methods as rectangle<double>.

Public, move-only class representing a PDF destination (a navigational target on a page) in the poppler namespace. It exposes the destination type (type_enum) and coordinate/zoom parameters and whether certain values should change. Non-copyable via poppler::noncopyable; movable. It holds a unique_ptr to an internal implementation (destination_private) and has a private constructor taking that pointer, implying construction is performed by friend class document or internal factory functions. Destructor is declared; ownership of internal data is managed via unique_ptr.

objects.definition:
enum type_enum
    {
        unknown,
        xyz,
        fit,
        fit_h,
        fit_v,
        fit_r,
        fit_b,
        fit_b_h,
        fit_b_v
    };
objects.description: Scoped enumeration nested in poppler::destination describing the kind of PDF destination: unknown, XYZ (explicit left/top/zoom), Fit (fit entire page), FitH (fit horizontal), FitV (fit vertical), FitR (fit rectangle), FitB (fit bounding box), FitBH (fit bounding box horizontal), FitBV (fit bounding box vertical). Exact behavioral details depend on the implementation; names follow PDF spec semantics.

Public value-type-like facade representing information about a font used in a PDF document: name, backing file path, embedding/subset flags, and font type. Backed by a private implementation (font_info_private) via a raw pointer. Copyable and assignable. The nested enum type_enum enumerates known font technologies and variants.

objects.definition:
enum type_enum
    {
        unknown,
        type1,
        type1c,
        type1c_ot,
        type3,
        truetype,
        truetype_ot,
        cid_type0,
        cid_type0c,
        cid_type0c_ot,
        cid_truetype,
        cid_truetype_ot
    };
objects.description: Enumeration of font technology/type classifications returned by font_info::type(). Values cover Type1/Type3/TrueType and CID-keyed variants, including OpenType-flavored forms. Defined as a nested enum inside poppler::font_info.

Non-copyable iterator that walks fonts used in a document, yielding vectors of font_info, presumably per page. Maintains current page index and uses a private implementation pointer. Constructible only by friend types (document/page), via a private constructor taking a page index/count and a document_private pointer.

Public C++ class representing a PDF document in the poppler namespace. It is non-copyable and provides access to document metadata, permissions, structure (pages, TOC), embedded files, fonts, destinations, and saving/loading. Construction is via static factory functions; instances manage internal state via a private implementation pointer.
Enumeration nested in poppler::document describing the initial page mode/view behavior for a PDF (e.g., show outlines/thumbnails, fullscreen).
Enumeration nested in poppler::document describing page layout hints for viewers (single page, one/two column, two page left/right).

A movable, non-copyable value-type-like wrapper around an internal text_box_data that represents a word-like chunk of text on a PDF page, with geometry, glyph bounding boxes, optional font info, and writing mode. Lifetime is independent but instances are produced and owned logically by page::text_list(). Destruction releases its unique_ptr-managed internal data.

Represents a single PDF page. Non-copyable. Provides page metadata (orientation, duration, label), geometry, text extraction, search, transition info, and access to text boxes. Internally uses a private implementation via page_private pointer. Instances are constructed internally (friend document) and destroyed via destructor.
Enumeration of writing modes for glyphs inside a text_box: invalid, horizontal, or vertical.
Orientation of a page: landscape, portrait, seascape (rotated 180 from landscape), or upside_down (rotated 180 from portrait).
Controls the search direction for page::search: start from top, next result, or previous result.
Text extraction layout mode: physical layout, raw order, or a hybrid non-raw-non-physical mode.
Bitmask flags for page::text_list; currently supports including font information in text boxes.
Forward-declared opaque structure holding the implementation data for text_box. No definition present in this header.
Forward declaration of the poppler::document class. Not defined in this header.
Forward declaration of the private implementation class for document. Not defined in this header.
Forward declaration of the private implementation class for page. Not defined in this header.
Forward declaration of a class describing page transition effects (for presentations). Not defined in this header.

Concrete image container class in namespace poppler. Owns pixel data (via pimpl pointer image_private) and provides basic inspection (format/width/height/stride), data access, copying, saving to disk, and listing supported file formats. Uses an internal implicit‑sharing/detach pattern suggested by the private pointer and detach(). Construction is via default, by size/format, or by adopting external data pointer. Details of memory ownership, lifetime, and deep/shallow copy semantics are not fully specified here; expect copy-on-write managed by image_private.

Enumeration of pixel storage formats used by poppler::image. Values indicate invalid image, 1-bit mono, 24-bit RGB, 32-bit ARGB, 8-bit grayscale, and 24-bit BGR respectively. It is a nested enum inside poppler::image.
Forward declaration of the private implementation class for poppler::image (pimpl). No definition is provided in this header; implementation details are hidden.

C++ class representing a PDF page transition in Poppler. Provides accessors for transition properties (type, duration, alignment, direction, angle, scale, rectangular flag). It follows the PIMPL pattern via page_transition_private and has a private constructor from an internal Object*, making it constructible only by friend class page; users can copy, assign, and destroy. Details of memory management for the private data are hidden and handled internally.

objects.definition:
enum type_enum
    {
        replace = 0,
        split,
        blinds,
        box,
        wipe,
        dissolve,
        glitter,
        fly,
        push,
        cover,
        uncover,
        fade
    };
objects.description: Enumeration of transition effect types supported for page transitions. Values map to PDF transition types such as split, wipe, dissolve, etc.
Enumeration for the alignment/orientation used by certain transition effects (horizontal or vertical).
Enumeration for the directionality of a transition (inward vs outward).
Forward declaration of the poppler::page class. No definition is provided in this header; it is referenced as a friend of page_transition. Details unknown here.
Forward declaration of a class named Object from outside the poppler namespace (likely a Poppler internal PDF object). Only referenced for a private constructor parameter; no definition present here.
Forward declaration of the private implementation (PIMPL) class for page_transition. Definition is not provided here.
Unsigned 32-bit integer typedef used to represent an ARGB color value in the poppler namespace (alpha, red, green, blue). Exact channel layout/endianness is not specified here.

Configurable renderer for poppler::page instances. Provides control over paper color, image format, render hints (antialiasing, text antialiasing, text hinting), and line rendering mode. Non-copyable; holds a private implementation pointer (page_renderer_private).
Bitmask flags controlling rendering behavior within page_renderer: enables general antialiasing, text antialiasing, and glyph hinting. Intended to be OR-ed into an unsigned int hints value.
Specifies how vector lines are rendered by page_renderer: default engine behavior, forced solid lines, or shape-based rendering for improved joins/caps at potential performance cost.
Forward declaration of poppler::page. Definition not present in this header; details unknown here.
Forward declaration of the private implementation class for page_renderer (PIMPL). Definition not present in this header; used solely via opaque pointer d.

Public non-copyable handle class in namespace poppler that represents an embedded file in a document. Provides accessors for metadata (name, unicode name, description, size, modification and creation times, MIME type), integrity (checksum), raw data, and validity. Destruction is via its destructor; construction is not public, implying instances are created internally (likely via embedded_file_private). The class uses a pimpl pointer (embedded_file_private *d) for implementation hiding.
Forward-declared private implementation class for poppler::embedded_file (PIMPL). Not defined in this header; serves to hide implementation details. No public API here.

Top-level Table-of-Contents handle for poppler. Non-copyable; constructed internally (private ctor) and destroyed via its destructor. Provides access to the root toc_item of the document TOC. Holds a private implementation pointer (toc_private *d). Details of construction and ownership are not exposed in this header.

Represents a single node in the document Table of Contents. Non-copyable; managed by toc. Exposes title, expansion state (is_open), and access to children via a vector snapshot or const iterators. Backed by a private implementation (toc_item_private *d). Construction is private; instances are provided by toc and internal code.
Forward declaration of the private implementation type for poppler::toc. No definition in this header; details unknown.
Forward declaration of the private implementation type for poppler::toc_item. No definition in this header; details unknown.

Iterator typedef aliasing std::vector<poppler::toc_item*> const_iterator, used to iterate over a toc_item's children. Pointer form requested; underlying is an iterator type from the standard library. Construction details follow std::vector const_iterator semantics.

functions.name: poppler::detail::noncopyable::noncopyable
functions.description: Default constructor for the noncopyable base class used to disable copying. It is protected; intended to be constructed only by derived classes.
requirements: May only be called from within constructors of classes deriving from poppler::detail::noncopyable (constructor is protected).
Objects of this type are intended as a base subobject; do not attempt to instantiate directly from outside derived classes.

functions.name: poppler::detail::noncopyable::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator is explicitly deleted to prevent assignment of noncopyable. Any attempt to copy-assign will be a compile-time error.
requirements: Callers must not attempt to copy-assign poppler::detail::noncopyable or derived classes that inherit this operator; this operator is deleted and cannot be used.

functions.name: poppler::ustring::ustring
functions.description: Default constructor for a UTF-16-based string type (inherits std::basic_string<char16_t>). Creates an empty ustring.
requirements: No special requirements; constructs an empty string.

functions.name: poppler::ustring::~ustring
functions.description: Destructor for ustring. Releases any owned resources.
requirements: The ustring object must be valid and not previously destroyed.

functions.name: poppler::ustring::to_utf8
functions.description: Returns a UTF-8 encoded copy of the string content as a byte_array (std::vector<char>). Useful for interfacing with APIs expecting UTF-8.
requirements: The ustring instance must be properly constructed.
Returned buffer should be treated as immutable copy; caller owns the returned byte_array.

functions.name: poppler::ustring::to_latin1
functions.description: Returns a Latin-1 (ISO-8859-1) encoded std::string representation of the ustring. Behavior for code points not representable in Latin-1 is not specified in this header.
requirements: The ustring instance must be properly constructed.
Caller should be aware that non-Latin-1 code points may be transformed or lost (unspecified).

functions.name: poppler::ustring::from_utf8
functions.signature: static poppler::ustring poppler::ustring::from_utf8(const char *str, int len = -1)
functions.description: Creates a ustring from a UTF-8 input buffer. If len is -1, str is treated as a null-terminated C string; otherwise, exactly len bytes are read. Intended to import UTF-8 text into the UTF-16-based ustring.
requirements: If len == -1, str must be a valid, null-terminated pointer to UTF-8 encoded bytes.
If len >= 0, str must point to a buffer of at least len bytes; the bytes are interpreted as UTF-8.
Behavior on invalid UTF-8 sequences is not specified in this header; callers should ensure valid UTF-8 or be prepared for failure/unspecified conversion results.
Passing a null pointer is invalid unless documented elsewhere (unspecified here).

functions.name: poppler::ustring::from_latin1
functions.description: Creates a ustring by converting a Latin-1 (ISO-8859-1) encoded std::string to UTF-16. Useful when input text is known to be Latin-1.
requirements: str should contain Latin-1 encoded bytes; behavior for values outside 0x00–0xFF is not applicable.
Behavior on inputs containing bytes that are not meaningful Latin-1 text is not specified; callers should ensure encoding correctness.

functions.name: poppler::convert_date_t
functions.description: Converts a date string to a time_t value. In the context of Poppler, this typically parses PDF date strings. Exact accepted formats and error handling are not specified in this header.
requirements: date should be a string in a format accepted by the implementation (likely a PDF date format, e.g., "D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSS..."), but exact requirements are unspecified.
Callers should handle cases where parsing fails or yields an unexpected time value (behavior unspecified here).

functions.name: poppler::operator<<
functions.description: Streams the contents of a byte_array (std::vector<char>) to an std::ostream. Intended to make byte_array printable/loggable.
requirements: stream must be a valid std::ostream reference.
array must be a valid byte_array; contents are read-only.
Callers should check the stream state after insertion to detect I/O errors.

functions.name: poppler::set_data_dir
functions.description: Sets the Poppler data directory path used to locate runtime resources. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
requirements: new_data_dir should be a valid filesystem path string understood by the implementation (exact expectations unspecified).
Callers should check the boolean return value to ensure the directory was accepted.

functions.name: poppler::set_debug_error_function
functions.description: Registers a callback function to receive debug/error messages from the library, with an opaque closure pointer passed back on invocation.
requirements: debug_function must match the signature void (*)(const std::string &, void *). Whether a null pointer is allowed to clear the handler is unspecified in this header.
closure must remain valid for as long as the callback may be invoked by the library; lifetime management is the caller’s responsibility.
Thread-safety and call context (e.g., which threads may invoke the callback) are unspecified; callbacks should be reentrant and avoid throwing exceptions.

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::rectangle
functions.description: Default constructor for a templated axis-aligned rectangle. Initializes all coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2) using T’s default constructor, resulting in a rectangle located at the origin with zero width and height for most arithmetic types.
requirements: Template parameter T must be default-constructible.
Instantiating this template requires T to be usable as a coordinate type (no additional constraints beyond default construction for this overload).

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::~rectangle
functions.description: Defaulted destructor for the templated rectangle. Performs no custom cleanup.
requirements: T must be destructible (required for any template instantiation).

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::is_empty
functions.description: Returns true if the rectangle is empty, defined as x1 == x2 and y1 == y2 (zero width and height).
requirements: Template parameter T must support operator==.

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::x
functions.description: Returns the x-coordinate of the rectangle’s top-left (stored as x1).
requirements: Template parameter T must be copyable (returned by value).

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::y
functions.description: Returns the y-coordinate of the rectangle’s top-left (stored as y1).
requirements: Template parameter T must be copyable (returned by value).

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::width
functions.description: Returns the width computed as x2 - x1. May be negative if the rectangle was constructed or modified with decreasing coordinates.
requirements: Template parameter T must support operator- and be copyable.

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::height
functions.description: Returns the height computed as y2 - y1. May be negative if the rectangle was constructed or modified with decreasing coordinates.
requirements: Template parameter T must support operator- and be copyable.

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::left
functions.description: Returns the left (minimum x) coordinate, x1.
requirements: Template parameter T must be copyable (returned by value).

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::top
functions.description: Returns the top (minimum y) coordinate, y1.
requirements: Template parameter T must be copyable (returned by value).

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::right
functions.description: Returns the right (maximum x) coordinate, x2.
requirements: Template parameter T must be copyable (returned by value).

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::bottom
functions.description: Returns the bottom (maximum y) coordinate, y2.
requirements: Template parameter T must be copyable (returned by value).

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::set_left
functions.description: Sets the left (x1) coordinate to value.
requirements: Template parameter T must be assignable to x1 (copy-assignable).
No normalization is performed; callers must ensure any intended invariants (e.g., left <= right) themselves if required by downstream code.

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::set_top
functions.description: Sets the top (y1) coordinate to value.
requirements: Template parameter T must be assignable to y1 (copy-assignable).
No normalization is performed; callers must ensure any intended invariants (e.g., top <= bottom) themselves if required by downstream code.

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::set_right
functions.description: Sets the right (x2) coordinate to value.
requirements: Template parameter T must be assignable to x2 (copy-assignable).
No normalization is performed; callers must ensure any intended invariants (e.g., left <= right) themselves if required by downstream code.

functions.name: poppler::rectangle::set_bottom
functions.description: Sets the bottom (y2) coordinate to value.
requirements: Template parameter T must be assignable to y2 (copy-assignable).
No normalization is performed; callers must ensure any intended invariants (e.g., top <= bottom) themselves if required by downstream code.

functions.name: poppler::operator<<
functions.signature: POPPLER_CPP_EXPORT std::ostream & poppler::operator<<(std::ostream &stream, const poppler::rect r)
functions.description: Stream insertion operator to print a poppler::rect (rectangle<int>) to an output stream. Intended for debugging or logging formatted rectangle data. Exact output format is not specified in the header.
requirements: stream must be a valid reference to a std::ostream open for output.
The rect argument is passed by value; it must be a valid, initialized rectangle<int>.
Callers should check the returned std::ostream& for error state if needed.

functions.name: poppler::destination::~destination
functions.description: Destructor for poppler::destination. Releases the internal destination_private state and associated resources. Typically invoked implicitly when a destination object goes out of scope.
requirements: The object must have been properly constructed before destruction.
Do not use the object after it has been destroyed.
No guarantees beyond standard C++ object lifetime; exception behavior is unspecified (no noexcept annotation in header).

functions.name: poppler::destination::destination
functions.description: Move constructor. Constructs a destination by taking ownership of the internal state from another destination instance. Intended for efficient transfers without copying.
requirements: other must be an rvalue (used in a move context).
After the move, other remains in a valid but unspecified state; do not rely on its data.
Operation is noexcept as per signature.

functions.name: poppler::destination::type
functions.description: Returns the destination type (e.g., xyz, fit, fit_h, fit_v, fit_r, fit_b, fit_b_h, fit_b_v, or unknown). Use this to interpret which of the coordinate/zoom fields are meaningful.
requirements: The destination object must be properly initialized (constructed by the library).
Callers should branch on the returned type to decide which coordinate fields are applicable; exact applicability per type is not specified in this header.

functions.name: poppler::destination::page_number
functions.description: Returns the 0-based or 1-based page index for the destination (exact base is not stated in this header). Typically identifies the target page within the document.
requirements: The destination must be valid/initialized.
Index base (0 vs 1) is unknown from this header; callers should consult library documentation or validate at runtime.

functions.name: poppler::destination::left
functions.description: Returns the left (x) coordinate associated with the destination, when applicable for the destination type. Coordinates are likely in PDF user space units; exact units are not specified here.
requirements: The destination must be valid/initialized.
Meaningfulness depends on destination type; for some types this value may be ignored.
Units and coordinate origin are not specified in this header; callers should not assume specific units without consulting documentation.

functions.name: poppler::destination::bottom
functions.description: Returns the bottom (y) coordinate associated with the destination, when applicable for the destination type. Coordinates likely reflect PDF user space; details not specified here.
requirements: The destination must be valid/initialized.
Meaningfulness depends on destination type; for some types this value may be ignored.
Units and coordinate origin are unspecified in this header.

functions.name: poppler::destination::right
functions.description: Returns the right (x) coordinate associated with the destination, when applicable (e.g., fit_r).
requirements: The destination must be valid/initialized.
Meaningfulness depends on destination type; for some types this value may be ignored.
Units are not specified in this header.

functions.name: poppler::destination::top
functions.description: Returns the top (y) coordinate associated with the destination, when applicable for the destination type.
requirements: The destination must be valid/initialized.
Meaningfulness depends on destination type; for some types this value may be ignored.
Units are not specified in this header.

functions.name: poppler::destination::zoom
functions.description: Returns the zoom/magnification factor for the destination, when applicable (e.g., xyz).
requirements: The destination must be valid/initialized.
Meaningfulness depends on destination type; for some types this value may be ignored.
Range/units (e.g., 1.0 = 100%) are not specified in this header.

functions.name: poppler::destination::is_change_left
functions.description: Indicates whether the left (x) coordinate should be applied/changed when navigating to this destination. Useful to distinguish between "keep current" and "set specific" behavior.
requirements: The destination must be valid/initialized.
Interpretation should be combined with the destination type to determine applicability of left().

functions.name: poppler::destination::is_change_top
functions.description: Indicates whether the top (y) coordinate should be applied/changed when navigating to this destination.
requirements: The destination must be valid/initialized.
Interpretation should be combined with the destination type to determine applicability of top().

functions.name: poppler::destination::is_change_zoom
functions.description: Indicates whether the zoom factor should be applied/changed when navigating to this destination.
requirements: The destination must be valid/initialized.
Interpretation should be combined with the destination type to determine applicability of zoom().

functions.name: poppler::destination::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Replaces this destination's internal state by taking ownership from other, releasing any previously held state.
requirements: other must be an rvalue (used in a move context).
Self-assignment with the same object in a move context results in a valid object, but the post-conditions for a moved-from object remain unspecified.
After the move, other is valid but holds an unspecified state; do not use its data.
Operation is noexcept as per signature.

functions.name: poppler::font_info::font_info
functions.description: Default constructor for a font_info object. Creates an instance representing information about a font discovered in a PDF document. Typically obtained indirectly via font_iterator or related APIs.
requirements: Must be invoked on a valid storage location (e.g., automatic, static, or dynamic).
The resulting object should not be used after it has been destroyed.

functions.name: poppler::font_info::font_info
functions.description: Copy constructor. Creates a new font_info as a copy of another.
requirements: Source object fi must refer to a valid, initialized font_info instance.
The resulting object should not be used after either object is destroyed.
Copying preserves the referenced font metadata; no additional preconditions are stated.

functions.name: poppler::font_info::~font_info
functions.description: Destructor for font_info. Releases resources associated with the font information instance.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
Ensure no references or pointers to internal data outlive the object.

functions.name: poppler::font_info::name
functions.description: Returns the font’s PostScript or internal name as a std::string. Intended for identifying the font found in the document.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, initialized font_info instance.
No mutation of the object occurs; method is const.

functions.name: poppler::font_info::file
functions.description: Returns the path or identifier of the font file associated with this font_info, if available. Useful for locating the external font resource.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, initialized font_info instance.
Return value may be an empty string when no external file is associated (e.g., embedded fonts); callers should handle empty results.

functions.name: poppler::font_info::is_embedded
functions.description: Indicates whether the font is embedded in the PDF document.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, initialized font_info instance.

functions.name: poppler::font_info::is_subset
functions.description: Indicates whether the font is subset (i.e., only a subset of glyphs is embedded).
requirements: Must be called on a valid, initialized font_info instance.

functions.name: poppler::font_info::type
functions.description: Returns the font type classification (Type1, TrueType, CID variants, etc.) as a font_info::type_enum.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, initialized font_info instance.
Callers should handle the type_enum::unknown case.

functions.name: poppler::font_info::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Replaces the contents of this font_info with those of another.
requirements: Both this and fi must be valid, initialized font_info instances.
Self-assignment should be supported but callers should avoid unnecessary self-assignment.
After assignment, previously held resources of the target may be released; do not use stale references obtained before assignment.

functions.name: poppler::font_iterator::~font_iterator
functions.description: Destructor for font_iterator. Cleans up iteration state over fonts in a document or page.
requirements: Do not use the iterator after destruction.
Ensure no outstanding references into the iterator’s internal state outlive it.

functions.name: poppler::font_iterator::next
functions.description: Advances the iterator and returns a batch of font_info entries discovered at the current position (commonly for the current page or segment). Intended to be called repeatedly until has_next() is false.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, live font_iterator instance.
Callers should check has_next() before calling next() to avoid advancing past the end.
The returned vector contains copies of font_info; manage them independently of the iterator’s lifetime.

functions.name: poppler::font_iterator::has_next
functions.description: Reports whether further batches of font_info are available from the iterator.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, live font_iterator instance.
Use the result to guard calls to next().

functions.name: poppler::font_iterator::current_page
functions.description: Returns the zero-based index (inferred) of the current page associated with the iterator’s position. Useful for correlating returned fonts to a specific page.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, live font_iterator instance.
Callers should not assume any specific starting value beyond typical zero-based indexing; handle unknown/implementation-defined values.

functions.name: poppler::document::~document
functions.description: Destructor for a poppler::document. Releases all resources associated with the document instance.
requirements: The document object must have been created via one of the load_from_* functions or other valid constructors in the library.
Do not use the document object after destruction.

functions.name: poppler::document::is_locked
functions.description: Returns whether the document is currently locked (i.e., requires a password to access content).

functions.name: poppler::document::unlock
functions.description: Attempts to unlock the document using the provided owner and/or user password. Returns true on success.
requirements: Caller may pass empty strings when a password is not available or not needed.
Should be called on a loaded document; behavior on an already-unlocked document is library-defined (unknown).

functions.name: poppler::document::page_mode
functions.description: Returns the document’s page mode (viewer’s initial mode), such as outlines, thumbnails, fullscreen, etc.

functions.name: poppler::document::page_layout
functions.description: Returns the document’s page layout preference (e.g., single page, one column, two-column).

functions.name: poppler::document::get_pdf_version
functions.description: Writes the PDF version of the document into the provided major and minor integers.
requirements: major must be a valid, writable pointer (non-null).
minor must be a valid, writable pointer (non-null).

functions.name: poppler::document::info_keys
functions.description: Returns the list of available document info dictionary keys.

functions.name: poppler::document::info_key
functions.description: Returns the value of the given info dictionary key as a ustring.
requirements: key identifies a valid info dictionary entry; behavior for unknown keys is library-defined (unknown).

functions.name: poppler::document::set_info_key
functions.description: Sets a document info dictionary key to the specified value. Returns true on success.
requirements: key should be a supported info key; unsupported keys may cause failure (exact set of keys is unknown).

functions.name: poppler::document::info_date_t
functions.description: Returns the date value associated with the given info key as a time_t.
requirements: key must refer to a date-type info key; behavior for non-date keys or missing keys is library-defined (unknown).

functions.name: poppler::document::set_info_date_t

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets UTF-8 text inputs consumed by the fuzz stubs:
# - poppler::ustring::from_utf8(ptr, len)
# - document metadata setters via ustring::from_utf8
# - page::create_page(label) via ustring::from_utf8
# - page::search(query) via ustring::from_utf8 with explicit length
# Strategy:
# Produce a concise, valid UTF-8 byte string that mixes:
# - ASCII words and punctuation
# - Latin-1 supplement, Greek, Cyrillic
# - CJK, emoji, RTL scripts
# - PDF-like date strings and metadata-like snippets (Title/Author, etc.)
# - Page label patterns (Roman numerals, Arabic, prefixed labels)
# The buffer is a single UTF-8 payload used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR(), so we concatenate
# several segments with separators. Always keep size <= 4096.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

_ASCII_WORDS = [
    "Hello", "world", "Poppler", "PDF", "Search", "Title", "Author",
    "Subject", "Keywords", "Creator", "Producer", "Label", "Page",
    "Unicode", "UTF-8", "Test", "Example", "Metadata", "Bookmark",
]

_ASCII_PUNCT = [" ", "\n", "\t", ", ", ". ", "; ", " - ", " | "]

# Useful date formats often seen in PDFs
_PDF_DATE_SAMPLES = [
    "D:20250101123045Z",
    "D:19991231235959+01'00'",
    "D:20050704010203-05'00'",
]

# Common metadata labels
_META_KEYS = [
    "Title", "Author", "Subject", "Keywords", "Creator", "Producer",
]

# Page label patterns, including roman numerals and sectioned labels
_ROMANS = ["i", "ii", "iii", "iv", "v", "vi", "vii", "viii", "ix", "x",
           "I", "II", "III", "IV", "V", "VI", "VII", "VIII", "IX", "X"]

# Non-ASCII code point pools for diversity
_LATIN1 = [
    " café", " naïve", " façade", " über", " señor", " año", " piñata",
]
_GREEK = [" Ελληνικά", " Αθήνα", " αβγ", " Δοκιμή"]
_CYRIL = [" Привет", " мир", " Москва", " тест"]
_CJK = [" 你好", " 世界", " 東京", " 京都", " 上海", " 測試", " 試験"]
_EMOJI = [" 😀", " 🧪", " 📄", " 🔍", " 🖨️", " 📝", " ✨", " 📎"]
_RTL = [" مرحبا", " بالعالم", " اختبار", " وثيقة"]

# Construct segments helpers

def rand_ascii_word(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(_ASCII_WORDS)

def rand_punct(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(_ASCII_PUNCT)

def rand_meta_line(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    key = rng.choice(_META_KEYS)
    val_parts: List[str] = []
    # Mix ASCII + non-ASCII parts
    val_parts.append(rand_ascii_word(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        val_parts.append(rng.choice(_LATIN1))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        val_parts.append(rng.choice(_GREEK))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        val_parts.append(rng.choice(_CYRIL))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        val_parts.append(rng.choice(_CJK))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        val_parts.append(rng.choice(_EMOJI))
    # Occasionally include RTL words (kept LTR in logical order)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        val_parts.append(rng.choice(_RTL))
    value = "".join(val_parts)
    return f"{key}: {value}\n"

def rand_pdf_date(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return rng.choice(_PDF_DATE_SAMPLES)
    # Build a loosely valid PDF date
    year = rng.randrange(1900, 2099)
    mon = rng.randrange(1, 13)
    day = rng.randrange(1, 29)
    hh = rng.randrange(0, 24)
    mm = rng.randrange(0, 60)
    ss = rng.randrange(0, 60)
    tz_mode = rng.random()
    if tz_mode < 0.34:
        tz = "Z"
    elif tz_mode < 0.67:
        offh = rng.randrange(0, 12)
        offm = rng.choice([0, 15, 30, 45])
        tz = f"+{offh:02d}'{offm:02d}'"
    else:
        offh = rng.randrange(0, 12)
        offm = rng.choice([0, 15, 30, 45])
        tz = f"-{offh:02d}'{offm:02d}'"
    return f"D:{year:04d}{mon:02d}{day:02d}{hh:02d}{mm:02d}{ss:02d}{tz}"

def rand_page_label(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    mode = rng.randrange(4)
    if mode == 0:
        return rng.choice(_ROMANS)
    if mode == 1:
        return str(rng.randrange(1, 401))
    if mode == 2:
        prefix = rng.choice(["A-", "B-", "Sec-", "App-", "Fig-", "Tbl-"])
        return f"{prefix}{rng.randrange(1, 51)}"
    # Mixed label with unicode
    return rng.choice(["前", "附", "章", "頁"]) + str(rng.randrange(1, 21))

# Build a query suited for page::search: non-empty, varied

def rand_search_query(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = [rand_ascii_word(rng)]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(rng.choice([" ", "\n"]))
        parts.append(rng.choice(_CJK + _CYRIL + _GREEK + _LATIN1))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append(rng.choice(_EMOJI))
    # Keep it moderately short
    return "".join(parts)

# Assemble the full UTF-8 buffer

def build_payload(rng: random.Random, target_size: int) -> bytes:
    segs: List[str] = []

    # Version banner segment
    segs.append("Poppler UTF-8 Sample\n")

    # Metadata-like lines
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(3, 8)):
        segs.append(rand_meta_line(rng))

    # Date lines resembling PDF info dates
    for k in ["CreationDate", "ModDate", "CustomDate"]:
        segs.append(f"{k}: {rand_pdf_date(rng)}\n")

    # Page label candidates
    labels = [rand_page_label(rng) for _ in range(rng.randrange(2, 6))]
    segs.append("Labels:" + ", ".join(labels) + "\n")

    # Search queries pool
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(2, 5)):
        q = rand_search_query(rng)
        segs.append("Query: " + q + "\n")

    # Mixed paragraphs to ensure longer multi-script text
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(1, 3)):
        para_parts: List[str] = []
        for _ in range(rng.randrange(5, 12)):
            para_parts.append(rand_ascii_word(rng))
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                para_parts.append(rng.choice(_LATIN1 + _GREEK + _CYRIL + _CJK + _EMOJI))
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                para_parts.append(rand_punct(rng))
        segs.append("".join(para_parts) + "\n")

    # Optional RTL line
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        segs.append("RTL: " + rng.choice(_RTL) + "\n")

    # Assemble and trim to target size
    data = ("".join(segs)).encode("utf-8")
    if len(data) > target_size:
        # Trim carefully to avoid breaking a multibyte sequence: back off to a valid boundary
        cut = target_size
        while cut > 0 and (data[cut-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
            cut -= 1
        data = data[:cut]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for Latin-1 text inputs targeting poppler::ustring::from_latin1
# Important: Do not embed literal NUL bytes (\x00) directly in the source.
# Any NUL-containing sequences are constructed at runtime via bytes([...]).

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Useful Latin-1 byte ranges constructed without embedding NULs in source
ASCII_BYTES = bytes(range(0x20, 0x7F))               # printable ASCII
CONTROL_BYTES_NO_NUL = bytes(list(range(0x01, 0x20)) + [0x7F])  # exclude 0x00
EXTENDED_LATIN1 = bytes(range(0x80, 0x100))          # 0x80..0xFF
WHITESPACE = b" \t\r\n\f\v"
PUNCT = b"!\"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\\]^_`{|}~"
DIGITS = b"0123456789"
LETTERS = (string.ascii_letters).encode('ascii')

# Common ASCII words
COMMON_ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"Hello, World!", b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.", b"PDF", b"Poppler", b"Title", b"Author",
    b"Subject", b"Keywords", b"Creator", b"Producer",
]

# Extended Latin-1 words built at runtime via explicit byte values
COMMON_EXTENDED_WORDS = [
    bytes([0x43,0x61,0x66,0xE9]),                                 # Café
    bytes([0x6E,0x61,0xEF,0x76,0x65]),                             # naïve
    bytes([0x66,0x61,0xE7,0x61,0x64,0x65]),                        # façade
    bytes([0x72,0xF4,0x6C,0x65]),                                  # rôle
    bytes([0x63,0x6F,0xF6,0x70,0x65,0x72,0x61,0x74,0x65]),         # coöperate
    bytes([0x47,0xF6,0x74,0x74,0x65,0x72,0x64,0xE4,0x6D,0x6D,0x65,0x72,0x75,0x6E,0x67]), # Götterdämmerung
    bytes([0x45,0x6C,0x20,0x6E,0x69,0xF1,0x6F,0x20,0x74,0x72,0x61,0x65,0x20,0x6D,0x61,0xF1,0x61,0x6E,0x61]), # El niño trae mañana
]

COMMON_WORDS_LATIN1 = COMMON_ASCII_WORDS + COMMON_EXTENDED_WORDS

# PDF-like tokens that might be searched later
PDF_TOKENS = [
    b"%PDF-1.7", b"/Title", b"/Author", b"/Subject", b"/Keywords", b"/Creator", b"/Producer", b"/Info",
    b"D:20250101000000Z", b"BT", b"ET", b"TJ", b"Tm", b"Tj"
]


def _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng: random.Random, pool: bytes, length: int) -> bytes:
    if not pool or length <= 0:
        return b""
    return bytes(pool[rng.randrange(0, len(pool))] for _ in range(length))


def _make_repeated_pattern(rng: random.Random, base: bytes, min_rep: int = 1, max_rep: int = 64, max_len: int = 1024) -> bytes:
    reps = rng.randint(min_rep, max_rep)
    out = base * reps
    if len(out) > max_len:
        out = out[:max_len]
    return out


def _mix_segments(rng: random.Random, parts: List[bytes], target_len: int) -> bytes:
    rng.shuffle(parts)
    out = b"".join(parts)
    if len(out) < target_len:
        pad = _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, EXTENDED_LATIN1 + ASCII_BYTES, target_len - len(out))
        out += pad
    return out[:target_len]


def _edge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    samples = []
    samples.append(b"")  # empty
    samples.append(bytes([0x00]))  # single NUL constructed at runtime
    samples.append(bytes([0xFF]))  # max byte
    samples.append(bytes([0x7F]))  # DEL
    samples.append(bytes([0x00]) * 32)  # many NULs
    samples.append(bytes([0xFF]) * 32)  # many 0xFF
    samples.append(bytes([0x80]) * 32)  # boundary into extended set
    samples.append(bytes([0x1B]) + b"[31mRed" + bytes([0x1B]) + b"[0m")  # ESC controls
    samples.append(PDF_TOKENS[0])  # %PDF-1.7
    samples.append(b";".join(PDF_TOKENS))  # concatenated PDF markers
    samples.append(bytes([0xEF,0xBB,0xBF]) + b"UTF8? but treated as Latin-1")  # UTF-8 BOM bytes
    samples.append((LETTERS + WHITESPACE + DIGITS + PUNCT)[:256])  # broad ASCII coverage
    samples.append(_rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, CONTROL_BYTES_NO_NUL, 64) + b"TEXT" + _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, CONTROL_BYTES_NO_NUL, 64))
    samples.append(_rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, EXTENDED_LATIN1, 128))
    samples.append(_rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, ASCII_BYTES, 128))
    samples.append(_make_repeated_pattern(rng, b"A", 1, 1024, 2048))  # homogeneous ASCII
    samples.append(_make_repeated_pattern(rng, bytes([0xFF,0x00]), 1, 1024, 2048))  # alternating max/min
    # Accented words joined
    acc = b"; ".join(w for w in COMMON_WORDS_LATIN1 if w)
    samples.append(acc)
    return samples


def _biased_lengths(rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    sizes = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 512, 1000, 1024, 2048, 3072]
    for _ in range(10):
        sizes.append(rng.randint(5, 3500))
    sizes = [min(s, MAX_SIZE) for s in sizes]
    rng.shuffle(sizes)
    return sizes[:8]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    strategy = rng.choice([
        "edge", "random_ascii", "random_extended", "mixed", "pattern", "tokens", "controls", "words"
    ])

    target_len = rng.choice(_biased_lengths(rng))

    if strategy == "edge":
        sample = rng.choice(_edge_cases(rng))
        return sample[:MAX_SIZE]

    if strategy == "random_ascii":
        n = max(0, target_len)
        return _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, ASCII_BYTES + WHITESPACE, n)

    if strategy == "random_extended":
        n = max(0, target_len)
        pool = EXTENDED_LATIN1 + ASCII_BYTES + WHITESPACE + bytes([0x00])  # allow NUL via runtime construction
        return _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, pool, n)

    if strategy == "mixed":
        parts: List[bytes] = []
        meta_keys = [b"Title", b"Author", b"Subject", b"Keywords", b"Creator", b"Producer"]
        key = rng.choice(meta_keys)
        value_words = [rng.choice(COMMON_WORDS_LATIN1) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5))]
        value = b" ".join(value_words)
        parts.append(key + b": " + value + b"\n")
        parts.append(rng.choice(PDF_TOKENS) + b"\n")
        parts.append(_rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, EXTENDED_LATIN1, rng.randint(16, 64)))
        parts.append(_rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, ASCII_BYTES, rng.randint(32, 128)))
        parts.append(_rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, CONTROL_BYTES_NO_NUL, rng.randint(0, 8)))
        return _mix_segments(rng, parts, target_len)

    if strategy == "pattern":
        base = rng.choice([
            b"A", b"0", bytes([0x00]), bytes([0xFF]), b"ab", bytes([0xFF,0x00]), bytes([0x80,0x7F]), b"Lorem ", b"\n",
        ])
        out = _make_repeated_pattern(rng, base, 1, 4096 // max(1, len(base)), max_len=min(MAX_SIZE, max(16, target_len)))
        if len(out) < target_len:
            tail = _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, EXTENDED_LATIN1 + ASCII_BYTES + WHITESPACE + bytes([0x00]), target_len - len(out))
            out += tail
        return out[:MAX_SIZE]

    if strategy == "tokens":
        parts = []
        count = rng.randint(5, 20)
        for _ in range(count):
            parts.append(rng.choice(PDF_TOKENS))
            sep = _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, WHITESPACE + PUNCT, rng.randint(1, 3))
            parts.append(sep)
        data = b"".join(parts)
        data += _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, EXTENDED_LATIN1, rng.randint(16, 64))
        return data[:max(1, target_len, 64)][:MAX_SIZE]

    if strategy == "controls":
        n_ctrl = rng.randint(16, 128)
        n_vis = max(0, target_len - n_ctrl)
        data = _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, CONTROL_BYTES_NO_NUL + bytes([0x00]), n_ctrl) + _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, ASCII_BYTES + WHITESPACE, n_vis)
        return data[:MAX_SIZE]

    if strategy == "words":
        words = [rng.choice(COMMON_WORDS_LATIN1) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 20))]
        glue = rng.choice([b" ", b"\n", b"\t", b", ", b"; ", b" | "])
        data = glue.join(words)
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            data += glue + _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, DIGITS + PUNCT, rng.randint(5, 40))
        return data[:max(1, target_len, 32)][:MAX_SIZE]

    pool = CONTROL_BYTES_NO_NUL + WHITESPACE + ASCII_BYTES + EXTENDED_LATIN1 + bytes([0x00])
    return _rand_bytes_from_pool(rng, pool, target_len)

import random
import string
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

# Generator for Poppler PDF date strings to exercise poppler::convert_date_t
# Target typical format variants: "D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSSOHH'mm'" with optional pieces,
# different separators, missing fields, Zulu, and timezones with or without quotes/colon.

def _rand_digits(rng, n):
    return ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_year(rng):
    # PDF allows 4+ digits; keep 4 digits in a broad range
    return f"{rng.randint(0, 9999):04d}"

def _rand_month(rng):
    # 01-12, but sometimes out-of-range values appear; keep valid to be parsable
    return f"{rng.randint(1, 12):02d}"

def _rand_day(rng, year, month):
    # choose valid day for the month/year
    # fallback to 28 to avoid invalid; or compute real max day
    try:
        # find first day of next month, then step back one day
        m = int(month)
        y = int(year)
        if m == 12:
            dt = datetime(y + 1, 1, 1) - timedelta(days=1)
        else:
            dt = datetime(y, m + 1, 1) - timedelta(days=1)
        max_day = dt.day
    except Exception:
        max_day = 28
    return f"{rng.randint(1, max_day):02d}"

def _rand_hour(rng):
    return f"{rng.randint(0, 23):02d}"

def _rand_minsec(rng):
    return f"{rng.randint(0, 59):02d}"

def _rand_offset(rng):
    # Offset formats to try:
    # 1) Z
    # 2) +HH'mm' or -HH'mm'
    # 3) +HHmm (no quotes)
    # 4) +HH:MM (colon style)
    # 5) empty (no offset)
    style = rng.choices([0,1,2,3,4], weights=[1,4,2,2,1])[0]
    if style == 0:
        return 'Z'
    if style == 4:
        return ''
    sign = rng.choice(['+', '-'])
    hh = f"{rng.randint(0, 12):02d}"
    mm = f"{rng.randint(0, 59):02d}"
    if style == 1:
        return f"{sign}{hh}'{mm}'"
    if style == 2:
        return f"{sign}{hh}{mm}"
    if style == 3:
        return f"{sign}{hh}:{mm}"
    return ''

def _maybe(sep, cond):
    return sep if cond else ''

def _build_pdf_date(rng):
    # Choose a variant profile
    variant = rng.choices(
        [
            'full',         # D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSSOHH'mm'
            'partial',      # D:YYYYMM (and maybe more)
            'no_prefix',    # YYYYMMDDHHmmSSZ
            'spacey',       # D:YYYY MM DD HH mm SS OHH'mm'
            'colons',       # D:YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM
            'just_date',    # D:YYYYMMDD
            'year_only',    # D:YYYY
            'iso_like',     # 1998-12-23 19:52:00 -08:00
        ],
        weights=[5,3,2,1,2,2,1,1]
    )[0]

    year = _rand_year(rng)
    month = _rand_month(rng)
    day = _rand_day(rng, year, month)
    hour = _rand_hour(rng)
    minute = _rand_minsec(rng)
    second = _rand_minsec(rng)
    offset = _rand_offset(rng)

    if variant == 'full':
        # Optionally drop seconds or minutes to hit partial time parsing
        include_min = True
        include_sec = rng.random() < 0.85
        s = f"D:{year}{month}{day}{hour}{minute}"
        if include_sec:
            s += second
        s += offset
        return s

    if variant == 'partial':
        # Build up to a random granularity
        gran = rng.choice(['Y','YM','YMD','YMDH','YMDHM'])
        s = 'D:'
        s += year
        if gran in ('YM','YMD','YMDH','YMDHM'):
            s += month
        if gran in ('YMD','YMDH','YMDHM'):
            s += day
        if gran in ('YMDH','YMDHM'):
            s += hour
        if gran in ('YMDHM'):
            s += minute
        # maybe add offset even on partial
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s += _rand_offset(rng)
        return s

    if variant == 'no_prefix':
        core = f"{year}{month}{day}{hour}{minute}{second}"
        return core + offset

    if variant == 'spacey':
        # Insert spaces or separators between fields
        sep = rng.choice([' ', ':', '-', '/'])
        s = f"D:{year}{sep}{month}{sep}{day}{sep}{hour}{sep}{minute}"
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            s += sep + second
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            s += sep + offset
        return s

    if variant == 'colons':
        # RFC3339-like but with D: prefix
        s = f"D:{year}-{month}-{day}T{hour}:{minute}:{second}"
        # prefer +HH:MM or Z
        off = rng.choice([f"{rng.choice(['+','-'])}{_rand_digits(rng,2)}:{_rand_digits(rng,2)}", 'Z'])
        return s + off

    if variant == 'just_date':
        return f"D:{year}{month}{day}"

    if variant == 'year_only':
        return f"D:{year}"

    if variant == 'iso_like':
        s = f"{year}-{month}-{day} {hour}:{minute}:{second}"
        off = rng.choice([f" {rng.choice(['+','-'])}{_rand_digits(rng,2)}:{_rand_digits(rng,2)}", 'Z'])
        return s + off

    # Fallback to a valid full string
    return f"D:{year}{month}{day}{hour}{minute}{second}{offset}"

def _maybe_corrupt_but_validish(rng, s):
    # Keep inputs likely acceptable but cover edge whitespace/trailing text
    # Add parentheses or leading/trailing whitespace occasionally (PDF strings sometimes wrapped)
    # Avoid exceeding 4096 total size
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        s = '(' + s + ')'
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 3) + s + ' ' * rng.randint(0, 3)
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        s += rng.choice([' GMT', ' UTC'])
    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Produce a set of candidates and pick one diversified by seed
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    candidates = []
    for _ in range(count):
        s = _build_pdf_date(rng)
        s = _maybe_corrupt_but_validish(rng, s)
        candidates.append(s)

    # Join multiple candidates with newlines to seed multiple parses if harness splits
    payload = '\n'.join(candidates)
    b = payload.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    # Ensure within size limit
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b

# This generator targets Poppler C++ fuzz stubs that consume arbitrary byte buffers
# via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. The most impactful targets here are
# document::load_from_data and document::load_from_raw_data, which expect bytes that
# form a valid (small) PDF file. We therefore generate small but valid PDF files
# exercising different features (catalog, pages, page content, metadata, outlines,
# named destinations, embedded file streams), while keeping total size <= 4096.
# The output is a bytes object suitable for feeding to the fuzz stubs.

# Utilities to build compact PDF objects and xref
class PDFBuilder:
    def __init__(self):
        self.objs = []  # list of (num, gen, data_bytes)
        self.offsets = []
        self.next_num = 1
        self.root_obj = None

    def add_obj(self, data: bytes, num: int | None = None):
        if num is None:
            num = self.next_num
            self.next_num += 1
        self.objs.append((num, 0, data))
        return num

    def set_root(self, num: int):
        self.root_obj = num

    def build(self) -> bytes:
        # Assemble a minimal valid PDF with xref and trailer
        out = bytearray()
        out += b"%PDF-1.5\n"  # reasonably new but widely supported
        # Add binary comment line to include high-bit chars
        out += b"%\xE2\xE3\xCF\xD3\n"
        self.offsets = [0] * (max(n for n,_,_ in self.objs) + 1)
        # sort objects by number
        self.objs.sort(key=lambda t: t[0])
        for (num, gen, data) in self.objs:
            self.offsets[num] = len(out)
            out += f"{num} {gen} obj\n".encode('ascii')
            out += data
            if not data.endswith(b"\n"):
                out += b"\n"
            out += b"endobj\n"
        xref_start = len(out)
        first = 0
        count = len(self.offsets)
        out += b"xref\n"
        out += f"{first} {count}\n".encode('ascii')
        # entry 0
        out += b"0000000000 65535 f \n"
        for i in range(1, count):
            off = self.offsets[i] if i < len(self.offsets) and self.offsets[i] else 0
            out += f"{off:010d} 00000 n \n".encode('ascii')
        # trailer
        out += b"trailer\n<<\n"
        size_line = f"/Size {count}\n".encode('ascii')
        out += size_line
        if self.root_obj is None:
            # fallback: set first object as root if not set
            if self.objs:
                self.root_obj = self.objs[0][0]
            else:
                # No objects; create a dummy empty catalog
                cat = self.add_obj(b"<< /Type /Catalog >>\n")
                self.root_obj = cat
        out += f"/Root {self.root_obj} 0 R\n".encode('ascii')
        out += b"/Info 2 0 R\n"  # if exists, fine; if not, compliant readers ignore unresolved but we'll ensure it exists below
        out += b">>\nstartxref\n"
        out += f"{xref_start}\n".encode('ascii')
        out += b"%%EOF\n"
        return bytes(out)


def rand_utf16le(seed: random.Random, max_chars: int) -> bytes:
    # produce UTF-16LE bytes (without BOM) suitable for ustring conversions when extracted
    n = seed.randint(1, max(1, max_chars))
    s = ''.join(chr(seed.randint(0x20, 0x7E)) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('utf-16le')


def make_stream(dict_entries: list[bytes], data: bytes) -> bytes:
    de = b"".join(dict_entries)
    d = b"<<" + de + f"/Length {len(data)}".encode('ascii') + b" >>\nstream\n" + data + b"\nendstream\n"
    return d


def build_min_pdf(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:

        + f"/Title (Tiny PDF {year}) /Author (Poppler Test) ".encode('ascii')

    emb_payload = ("Attachment seed=" + str(rng.randrange(1<<30))).encode('utf-8')

    filespec = pdf.add_obj(b"<< /Type /Filespec /F (att.txt) /EF << /F %d 0 R >> >>\n" % ef_stream)
    af_array = pdf.add_obj(b"[ %d 0 R ]\n" % filespec)

    # 10. Catalog
    cat_parts = []
    cat_parts.append(b"/Type /Catalog ")
    cat_parts.append(b"/Pages %d 0 R " % pages_num)
    cat_parts.append(b"/Outlines %d 0 R " % outlines)
    # Names dictionary containing Dests
    cat_parts.append(b"/Names << /Dests %d 0 R >> " % names_num)
    # Attachments (AF and Names/EmbeddedFiles)
    cat_parts.append(b"/AF %d 0 R " % af_array)
    # PageMode and PageLayout variations
    page_modes = [b"/PageMode /UseNone ", b"/PageMode /UseOutlines ", b"/PageMode /UseThumbs ", b"/PageMode /FullScreen "]
    cat_parts.append(rng.choice(page_modes))
    page_layouts = [b"/PageLayout /SinglePage ", b"/PageLayout /TwoColumnLeft ", b"/PageLayout /TwoPageRight "]
    cat_parts.append(rng.choice(page_layouts))
    cat = b"<< " + b"".join(cat_parts) + b" >>\n"
    cat_num = pdf.add_obj(cat)
    pdf.set_root(cat_num)

    return pdf.build()


def build_variants(seed: int) -> list[bytes]:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = []

    # Variant 1: minimal PDF with content, names/dests, outlines, embedded file
    out.append(build_min_pdf(rng))

    # Variant 2: same but uncompressed content stream to exercise raw parser
    rng2 = random.Random(seed ^ 0xA5A5_5A5A)

    font = pdf.add_obj(b"<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Times-Roman >>\n")
    res = pdf.add_obj(b"<< /Font << /F1 %d 0 R >> >>\n" % font)
    page = pdf.add_obj(b"<< /Type /Page /Parent 5 0 R /Resources %d 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 300 400] /Contents %d 0 R >>\n" % (res, cont))
    pdf.add_obj(b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [%d 0 R] /Count 1 >>\n" % page, num=5)
    cat = pdf.add_obj(b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 5 0 R >>\n")

    page3 = pdf3.add_obj(b"<< /Type /Page /Parent 5 0 R /Resources %d 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 10 10] /Contents %d 0 R >>\n" % (res3, cont3))
    pdf3.add_obj(b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [%d 0 R] /Count 1 >>\n" % page3, num=5)
    cat3 = pdf3.add_obj(b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 5 0 R >>\n")
    pdf3.set_root(cat3)
